title: Morning Brief — Wed 25 Nov

stories.board: New Trump tariffs coming; tech stocks slide
stories.headline: US gets ready for new tariffs, and tech stock futures drop
stories.what: The Trump team plans new tariffs (extra taxes on goods from other countries) on China, the EU and about 14 more places, maybe this week. Nasdaq futures (bets on where tech stocks will open) fell over 2 percent, and Nvidia fell about 5 percent before the bell.
stories.why: Tariffs can raise prices, and AI and chip stocks were already falling.
stories.sides: Bloomberg says the new tariffs will be targeted and no higher than trade-deal levels; right-leaning Townhall notes most voters in an exit poll said the trade war hurt the economy.

stories.board: Canada to Pentagon: We don't report to you
stories.headline: Canada pushes back after the Pentagon criticizes its military
stories.what: Defence Minister David McGuinty answered a Pentagon complaint about Canada's spending, ready-to-use equipment and its review of F-35 fighter jets. He said Canada is on track to spend 5 percent of GDP (the size of the whole economy) on defence by 2035.
stories.why: Canada and the US defend North America together through NORAD, so a fight between them matters.
stories.sides: Wire services and CTV report it plainly; right-leaning outlets say Canada fired back, and the Pentagon says it will do what it must if it cannot rely on Canada.

stories.headline: Israel's unity talks end another round without a deal
stories.what: Teams for Gadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu met again and agreed to keep talking, but still did not agree. They are stuck on who is prime minister first, whether Ben-Gvir's far-right party joins, and who picks the October 7 inquiry (an official investigation).
stories.why: Eisenkot has only until early December to build a government, or Israel may face more political trouble.
stories.sides: Eisenkot's side says Netanyahu is stalling; Likud says it wants a wide unity government; Eisenkot says he may form an emergency government without Likud.

quick_hits: Michigan has frozen permits for Enbridge's Line 5 oil pipeline tunnel, which carries Canadian oil.
The Weather Network expects a milder winter than usual across much of Canada.
US stock markets close Thursday for American Thanksgiving, and a key inflation report comes out this morning.
big_picture: Trade and defence fights with the US are back in the news, while Israel still waits for a new government.
